name: Galería de la Raza
funding: National Endowment for the Arts, California Arts Council, San Francisco Arts Commission, Mellon Foundation; 501(c)(3) non-profit.

name: Galerie de l'UQAM
funding: University gallery. Named partners: Canada Council for the Arts, CALQ and UQAM; donations go through the UQAM foundation.
records_note: The gallery posts nothing itself; parent UQAM posts annual reports from 2001-02 with financial results, and the gallery shows three undated partner logos.

name: Galerie Rudolfinum
records_note: Posts annual reports from 2012 to 2025 with revenue tables and partner logos, but no financial statements or board list.

name: GAMeC
funding: City of Bergamo, with corporate sponsors including SABO (manufacturer).
records_note: It posts yearly accounts for 2017 to 2025 that name 27 private funders for 2025, and lists its board, but no separate annual report.

name: Gaza Biennale
funding: 2024-25: aimed to raise $90,000 for artists; sponsor Al Risan Art Museum, plus small partners per pavilion and private donations.
watch: Decentralised, crowdfunded project; pavilion partners vary by city. It staged a protest at the ICA against Bloomberg in Jan 2025 and was not a target.
records_note: Its own site sits behind a bot check, so its reports, accounts, funders and board could not be checked; only press coverage was readable.

name: Geelong Gallery
funding: Revenue A$2.85M (2024-25) with grants A$1.67M, from the City of Greater Geelong and the Victorian Government, and sponsorship A$41k. Donors include the Ian Potter, Brookes, Archibald and Trawalla foundations.
watch: Nearly 70,000 visitors in 2024-25. The cited partners page dates from 2020-21; the annual report is current.
records_note: Posts six annual reports with audited accounts, names donors in the 2024-25 report and lists its board; the partners page is from 2020-21.

name: Georgia O'Keeffe Museum
funding: Founded with a $10M Burnett Foundation gift from Anne Marion.
watch: Anne Marion's Burnett fortune mixes ranching and oil; she chaired Burnett Oil Company. No current Burnett gift or controversy was found.
records_note: Its Financial Policy and Documents page posts 2025 audited statements and a 2024 Form 990, and a board page names 30 trustees; no donor list.

name: Gertrude Contemporary
funding: Creative Victoria, the federal Visual Arts, Craft and Design Framework and City of Darebin. Donors include Michael and Janet Buxton, Proclaim, and the Mori Provan and Tucker foundations.
watch: Proclaim has sponsored the Octopus exhibition since 2002. No flagged-industry funder.
records_note: Posts annual reports for 2023 to 2025 with a financial report and names board members; its supporters page names donors without a date.

name: GES-2 House of Culture
funding: Funded through the V-A-C Foundation, endowed by Leonid Mikhelson, CEO and key shareholder of Novatek, Russia's major natural gas producer.
watch: Opened Dec 2021 as Russia's largest private art centre. Artistic director Francesco Manacorda resigned Mar 2022. In 2023 Ural Biennial founder Alisa Prudnikova became its director. GES-2 also appears as a sponsor on the Tretyakov Gallery's 2026 partner list.
why_flagged: Opened Dec 2021 as Russia's largest private art centre. Artistic director Francesco Manacorda resigned Mar 2022. In 2023 Ural Biennial founder Alisa Prudnikova became its director. GES-2 also appears as a sponsor on the Tretyakov Gallery's 2026 partner list.
records_note: GES-2 posts no annual report, accounts, donor or sponsor list, or board; the site names only the founder Leonid Mikhelson.

name: Ghetto Biennale
watch: Biennial on the Grand Rue, Port-au-Prince; Atis Rezistans also took part in documenta fifteen in 2022. No controversy found.
records_note: Its edition pages name sponsors in text for 2015, 2017 and 2019, but there are no annual reports, accounts or board list.

name: Gibbes Museum of Art
funding: Carolina Art Association expenses $4.5M (2023); trustees, members, Art Bridges, SC Arts Commission, local banks and firms.
records_note: One annual report (FY2025) with a donor list, Form 990s for FY2024 and FY2025 on its site, and the board members listed.
